breadcrumb: Std 6 Social Science Term-III (English) — History Unit 3: The Age of Empires: Guptas and Vardhanas — Boxed notes (தெரிந்து தெளிவோம் / Do you know)

questions.quote: Prashasti is a Sanskrit word, meaning commendation or 'in praise of'. Court poets flattered their kings listing out their achievements. These accounts were later engraved on pillars so that the people could read them.

options: a code of laws for the kingdom
a guild of traders and bankers
en.explanation: Court poets listed the kings' achievements; these accounts were engraved on pillars.

ta.explanation: அவைக் கவிஞர்கள் அரசரின் சாதனைகளைப் பட்டியலிட்டுப் புகழ்ந்தனர்; அவை தூண்களில் பொறிக்கப்பட்டன.

questions.quote: Chandragupta I (319–335 AD(CE)) married Kumaradevi of the famous and powerful Lichchhavi family. The gold coins attributed to Chandragupta bear the images of Chandragupta, Kumaradevi and the legend 'Lichchhavayah'.

en.q: Chandragupta I married Kumaradevi of the ______ family.
en.explanation: The Lichchhavi was an old gana-sangha whose territory lay between the Ganges and the Nepal Terai.

ta.explanation: லிச்சாவி கங்கைக்கும் நேபாளத் தராய்க்கும் இடையிலிருந்த பழைய கணசங்கம்.

questions.quote: Samudragupta conquered nine kingdoms in northern India. He reduced 12 rulers of the southern India to the status of feudatories. He revived the Vedic practice of performing horse sacrifice. He issued gold coins and in one of them, he is portrayed playing harp (veenai).

en.q: In one of his gold coins, Samudragupta is portrayed playing the ______.
en.explanation: He earned the title 'Kaviraja' for his love of poetry and music.

ta.q: சமுத்திரகுப்தர் தம் தங்க நாணயம் ஒன்றில் ______ வாசிப்பவராகச் சித்தரிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளார்.

questions.quote: Chandragupta II (380 - 415 AD(CE)) was also known as Vikramaditya. He conquered western Malwa and Gujarat by defeating the Saka rulers. Vikramaditya is said to have assembled the greatest writers and artists (Navaratna [Nine Jewels]) in his court. Kalidasa is said to be one among them.

en.q: Chandragupta II, who defeated the Saka rulers of western Malwa and Gujarat, was also known as ______.
en.explanation: Navaratna (Nine Jewels) adorned his court; Kalidasa is said to be one of them.

ta.q: மேற்கு மாளவம், குஜராத்தின் சகர்களை வென்ற இரண்டாம் சந்திரகுப்தர் ______ எனவும் அழைக்கப்பட்டார்.
ta.explanation: அவர் அவையில் நவரத்தினங்கள் இருந்தன; காளிதாசர் அவருள் ஒருவர்.

questions.quote: Chandragupta II was succeeded by his son Kumaragupta I, who built the famous Nalanda University. Kumaragupta's successor Skandagupta had to face a new threat in the form of the invasion of Huns.

en.q: The famous Nalanda University was built by ______.
en.explanation: It flourished under the patronage of the Gupta Empire and later under Harsha.

ta.explanation: இது குப்தரின் ஆதரவிலும் பின்னர் ஹர்ஷர் ஆதரவிலும் செழித்தது.

questions.quote: The last recognised king of the Gupta Empire was Vishnugupta. The last of the great Guptas was Baladitya.

en.q: The last recognised king of the Gupta Empire was ______.
en.explanation: Baladitya was the last of the great Guptas.

questions.quote: Classification of land during Gupta period: Kshetra - cultivable land; Khila - waste land; Aprahata - jungle or forest land; Vasti - habitable land; Gapata Saraha - pastoral land.

en.q: In the Gupta land classification, 'Khila' meant ______.
en.explanation: Kshetra - cultivable land; Aprahata - forest; Vasti - habitable; Gapata Saraha - pastoral.

ta.explanation: க்ஷேத்ரம் - பயிர் நிலம்; அப்ரஹதம் - காடு; வஸ்தி - குடியிருப்பு நிலம்; கபத சரஹம் - மேய்ச்சல்.

questions.quote: There were two types of traders, namely Sresti and Sarthavaha. Sresti traders usually settled at a standard place. Sarthavaha traders were caravan traders who carried their goods to different places.

en.q: The caravan traders who carried goods to different places in the Gupta period were called ______.
en.explanation: Sresti traders usually settled at a standard place.

ta.q: குப்தர் காலத்தில் பல இடங்களுக்குப் பொருள்களைக் கொண்டு சென்ற வணிகக் குழுவினர் ______ எனப்பட்டனர்.
ta.explanation: ஸ்ரேஷ்டிகள் ஒரே இடத்தில் தங்கி வணிகம் செய்தனர்.

questions.quote: Huns were nomadic tribes, who, under their great Attila, were terrorising Rome and Constantinople. After defeating Skandagupta, they spread across Central India. Their chief, Toromana, crowned himself as king. After him, his son Mihirakula ruled. Finally, Yasodharman, ruler of Malwa, defeated them and ended their rule.

en.q: Who finally defeated the Huns and ended their rule in India?
en.explanation: Toromana's son Mihirakula had ruled the captured territories.

questions.quote: Nalanda University: At Nalanda, Buddhism was the main subject of study. Other subjects like Yoga, Vedic literature and Medicine were also taught. Eight Mahapatashalas and three large libraries were situated on the campus. Today, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

en.q: Which of the following was the main subject of study at Nalanda University?
en.explanation: Yoga, Vedic literature and Medicine were also taught.

questions.quote: Samudragupta introduced the Gupta monetary system. The Gupta gold coins were known as Dinara. Mining and metallurgy were the most flourishing industries during the Gupta period. The most important evidence of development in metallurgy was the Mehrauli Iron Pillar installed by King Chandragupta in Delhi.

en.q: The Gupta gold coins were known as ______.
en.explanation: Samudragupta introduced the Gupta monetary system, inspired by Kushana coins.

ta.explanation: குஷாணர் நாணயங்களின் தாக்கத்தில் சமுத்திரகுப்தர் நாணய முறையை அறிமுகப்படுத்தினார்.

questions.quote: The society that adhered to four varna system was patriarchal. According to laws of Manu, women should be under the protection of their father, husband or eldest son. Polygamy was widely prevalent. Sati was practised during the Gupta rule.

en.q: The laws followed in Gupta society, which said women should be under the protection of father, husband or eldest son, were the laws of ______.

ta.q: பெண்கள் தந்தை, கணவன், மூத்த மகனின் பாதுகாப்பில் இருக்க வேண்டும் என்ற குப்தர் கால விதிகள் ______ ன் சட்டங்கள்.

questions.quote: Kalidasa's famous dramas were Sakunthala, Malavikagnimitra and Vikramaoorvashiyam. Other significant works were Meghaduta, Raghuvamsa, Kumarasambava and Ritusamhara.

en.q: The Age of Empires: Guptas and Vardhanas: Which of the following is a work of Kalidasa?
en.explanation: Raghuvamsa, Kumarasambava and Ritusamhara are his other works.

ta.explanation: ரகுவம்சம், குமார சம்பவம், ருதுசம்ஹாரம் ஆகியவையும் அவர் படைப்புகள்.

questions.quote: The founder of the Vardhana or Pushyabhuti dynasty ruled from Thaneswar. Pushyabhuti served as a military general under the Guptas and rose to power after the fall of the Guptas. Rajavardhana, the eldest son of Prabhakaravardhana, ascended the throne.

en.explanation: Pushyabhuti served as a general under the Guptas.

questions.quote: The most popular king of the Vardhana dynasty was Harshavardhana. Harsha ruled for 41 years. It was Harsha who unified most of northern India. But the extension of his authority in the south was checked by Chalukya king Pulikesin II.

en.q: Harsha's extension of authority in the south was checked by the Chalukya king ______.
en.explanation: Harsha unified most of northern India.

ta.q: ஹர்ஷரின் தெற்கு நோக்கிய விரிவாக்கத்தைத் தடுத்த சாளுக்கிய மன்னன் ______.

questions.quote: Hiuen Tsang, the 'prince of pilgrims', visited India during Harsha's reign. His Si-Yu-Ki provides detailed information about the social, economic, religious and cultural conditions of India during Harsha's time.

en.q: Hiuen Tsang, the 'prince of pilgrims', wrote the travel account ______.
en.explanation: It describes the social, economic, religious and cultural conditions of Harsha's India.

ta.q: 'யாத்ரிகர்களின் இளவரசர்' ஹியூன்சாங் எழுதிய பயணக் குறிப்பு நூல் ______.
ta.explanation: இது ஹர்ஷர் கால இந்தியாவின் சமூக, பொருளாதார, சமய, பண்பாட்டு நிலைகளை விவரிக்கிறது.

questions.quote: He summoned two Buddhist assemblies, one at Kanauj and another at Prayag. In the assembly at Prayag, Harsha distributed his wealth among the Buddhists, Vedic scholars and poor people. Harsha was the last Buddhist sovereign in India.

en.q: Harsha summoned two Buddhist assemblies, one at Kanauj and the other at ______.
en.explanation: At Prayag he distributed his wealth to Buddhists, Vedic scholars and the poor.

ta.q: ஹர்ஷர் கனோஜ், ______ ஆகிய இடங்களில் இரு பௌத்தப் பேரவைகளைக் கூட்டினார்.
ta.explanation: பிரயாகையில் தம் செல்வத்தைப் பௌத்தர், வேத அறிஞர், ஏழைகளுக்கு வழங்கினார்.

questions.quote: Harsha's popular works are Ratnavali, Nagananda and Priyadharshika. His royal court was adorned by Banabhatta, Mayura, Hardatta and Jayasena. The Nalanda University had 10,000 students and monks in residence, when Hiuen Tsang visited.

en.q: Which of the following poets adorned Harsha's royal court?
en.explanation: Mayura, Hardatta and Jayasena were also in his court.

ta.q: பின்வரும் புலவர்களுள் ஹர்ஷர் அவையை அலங்கரித்தவர் யார்?
